repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == false)
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a rising-edge wait (`wait(MotionSensor.Motion == true, edge rising)`) which should fire exactly when the motion signal transitions from false to true. The candidate uses a periodic `if` check at the start of every cycle (1000 ms). At t=0, motion is false; at t=100 ms, motion becomes true. The candidate's `if` condition is evaluated only at t=0 (false) and t=1000 ms (motion is still true), missing the rising edge at t=100 ms. This matches Example A: polling misses the transition instant.
diagnosis.change_summary: Changed the script from a periodic polling `if` to a blocking rising-edge state machine. The new script waits for the rising edge, executes the body, and then blocks until the signal drops to false before waiting for the next rising edge. The period is set to the cycle duration (1 SEC) to match the IR's repeating behavior.
